ledger.claim: The GPS trace measures 13.2 km between the recorded pickup and the recorded dropoff against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 3.2 km or 32% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trace figure is the governing measurement under POL-RD-01 and it happens to agree with the trip record's convenience copy, so no conflict arises.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 104 fixes over 100% coverage at a 10-second sample interval, zero gaps, and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) fires, so the rider's proof needs no independent corroboration, excess is measured on the trace as recorded, and POL-RD-07(i) to (iii) and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-02838-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its absence is itself citable. POL-RD-03's comparison therefore cannot be run: there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, so no external traffic cause can reduce or excuse the 3.2 km excess, and any such excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13.

The one message on the trip is the rider's own 'changed the pin to the other building', sent at 14:06:43 after the meter started at 14:03:23, and it exonerates no distance. Its waypoint_hint is null and it names no road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and that clause is unavailable on the record; and even treated as an instruction, the trace never shows the vehicle travelling to the place it names, so under POL-RD-14 the instruction caused none of the measured excess and no distance is excluded.

The dropoff pin was amended at 14:07:23, but the trip record stores no amended optimal: amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 accordingly cannot be run, no substitute figure may be derived from the booked 10.0 km optimal, and neither the re-measurement nor the partial exclusion of pre-amendment distance can be applied. The excess stands at the measured 3.2 km for the POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 arithmetic.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. Trip identifier TRP-02838 appears on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown alike, and the excess is measured from a trace that is not impaired, so the burden shifts to the driver; the driver's counterparty statement ('Rider moved the pin') cites no evidence id and no clause and is discarded under POL-RD-08 as discharging nothing. The rider's own profile adds no corroboration requirement either: deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the POL-RD-08 threshold of 4, and POL-GEN-01 permits that field to be used for this test only.

The fare model on this trip is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route: the rider was billed per kilometre and per minute actually driven, and POL-RD-02 governs the remedy. The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary.

Running POL-RD-02 on the booked optimal route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.0 + 0.28 x 14.0) = 15.22, multiplied by the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, gives a recomputed fare of 16.02. Refund = 19.32 charged_total less 16.02 = 3.30, which is above the 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.30. Payment status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so this refund moves money the rider is presently carrying.

There is no pass-through line to correct, and none to count twice. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all, tolls_erp is 0.00, both the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are 0.00, and the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. The POL-RD-02 refund of 3.30 is therefore neither enlarged nor duplicated by POL-RD-09.

The billed distance is 13.2 km and the trace distance is 13.2 km, so the rider was billed for exactly the distance driven: there is no unbilled-distance shortfall and no DRIVER_COMPENSATION is available under POL-RD-04. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the booked 10.0 km optimal is the correct comparator.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger is engaged on this record. The trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare ledger; the trace is unimpaired with no gaps; the timestamps run forward; the refund of 3.30 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total. Limb (5) is not engaged either, because the driver's pin-move assertion cites no artifact and no clause, and an assertion that cites nothing cannot be invoked against a record field that no party has put in issue.

The drop-off point was relocated mid-trip, and the rider says so in her own words. trip_record.dropoff_amended_at reads 2026-08-12T14:07:23, and the only chat message on the trip, sent by the rider at 14:06:43, reads 'changed the pin to the other building'. Under POL-RD-05 the baseline for any deviation test is the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints, not the booked 10.0 km figure against which this rider's claim is measured.

The amended re-quote that POL-RD-05 requires is absent from the record: trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null even though dropoff_amended_at is set. POL-RD-05 provides that in exactly that state the clause cannot be run and the tribunal must not derive a substitute figure, and POL-RD-10(5) names 'a POL-RD-05 amendment with amended_optimal_distance_km null' as a mandatory escalation trigger. The case must go to a human reviewer, not produce a refund computed against the un-amended optimal route.

Escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal: it replaces the ruling, no monetary outcome issues, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. On a rider-filed dispute whose fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and whose refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, that is the outcome which leaves the driver's fare undisturbed pending human review instead of returning it.

The rider's prima facie case shifts the burden to the driver under POL-RD-08, and the driver discharges it by naming a specific artifact and a specific clause from the list POL-RD-08 gives: EV-TRIP-02838, whose amendment timestamps are the artifact, and POL-RD-05, the exculpatory clause. The driver asserts no uncited traffic excuse, so nothing turns on POL-RD-08's bar against bare assertion.

Even taking the rider's own trace figure at face value, the excess is 3.2 km over a 10.0 km booked optimal, 32%, which clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) but is not MATERIAL: POL-RD-01 sets materiality at more than 50% or more than 8.0 km absolute, and neither is met. The rider therefore cannot reach the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) on this trip's evidence, whatever else is decided.

Nor is any repeat-deviation pattern established under POL-RD-06: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the three-flag threshold, and 1 divided by 207 completed_trips_90d is about 0.005, far below the 0.05 ratio threshold. Those two fields are the only profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits for this test, so the rider's remedy cannot be uplifted to FULL_REFUND and no driver-conduct referral follows from the profile.

The escalation does not rest on trace impairment, and the tribunal should name the right trigger. The gps_trace is clean for policy purposes: 104 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) never fires and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The trigger that fires is POL-RD-10(5), the missing amended re-quote.

No traffic advisory covers this corridor: EV-ADVIS-02838-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the driver asserts no external traffic cause. Under POL-RD-13 an absent advisory that no party cites is a gap in the bundle, not the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction of 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory', so it neither exonerates nor incriminates the driver and supplies no second escalation trigger.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — rider and driver — in the dispute over trip TRP-02838 (Northpoint City to Blk 7 Everton Park, 12 August 2026).

This case goes to a human reviewer and no money moves today. The charge of SGD 19.32 stands as it is (EV-FARE-02838: payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded.

What the record shows. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02838 measures 13.2 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off against a booked optimal of 10.0 km on the trip record EV-TRIP-02838 — an excess of 3.2 km, or 32%, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km) but is not a MATERIAL deviation, which needs more than 50% or more than 8.0 km. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): 104 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds. On the trace alone the rider's case would be the ordinary POL-RD-02 partial refund: charged_total 19.32 less a recomputed fare of 16.02 (= (3.80 + 0.75 × 10.0 + 0.28 × 14.0) × the surge multiplier of 1.0 read on EV-FARE-02838, + 0.80 platform fee, no ERP, no surcharge, no waiting fee, no promo discount) = 3.30, above the 0.50 de minimis and well under 90% of charged_total.

What stops that computation. The trip record shows the drop-off pin was amended mid-trip — dropoff_amended_at = 2026-08-12T14:07:23, with the drop-off moved from the original pin (1.3563, 103.8545) to (1.3591, 103.8522) — and the rider confirms it in the only chat message of the trip (EV-CHAT-02838, 14:06:43, 'changed the pin to the other building'). POL-RD-05 requires the deviation to be re-measured against the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints, and it states that distance driven before the amendment is never counted as excess against the driver. That re-quote is not on the record: trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null even though the amendment timestamp is set. POL-RD-05 says in terms that in this state the clause cannot be run, that POL-RD-10(5) applies, and that no substitute figure may be derived. POL-RD-10(5) names 'a POL-RD-05 amendment with amended_optimal_distance_km null' as a mandatory escalation trigger, and POL-RD-10 is terminal: it replaces the ruling and no monetary outcome issues. It has fired, so I may not issue the 3.30 refund, and equally may not let the 19.32 stand as a final finding.

Claims answered. The rider's submission that the excess simply 'stands at the measured 3.2 km' because the amended re-quote is missing is rejected on its consequence: the missing re-quote is the escalation trigger, not a defect to be worked around, and the booked 10.0 km optimal cannot be used as though nothing had been amended. The rider's submission that no POL-RD-10 trigger is engaged because the driver cited nothing is also rejected: the driver's brief cites EV-TRIP-02838 and POL-RD-05, and the amendment is a fact of the record itself, not merely an assertion. The driver's counterparty statement ('Rider moved the pin') is consistent with the record but cites no evidence ID and carries no weight of its own under POL-RD-08. The rider's POL-RD-02 arithmetic (3.30) is correct as arithmetic and is not applied, because the baseline is put in issue by the un-run POL-RD-05. Both sides agree the trace is unimpaired and the trigger is POL-RD-10(5) rather than POL-RD-10(3); that is accepted.

Rest of the record, recorded for the reviewer. Trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-02838, EV-GPS-02838 and EV-FARE-02838, and the timestamps run forward. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02838-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the driver asserts no traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 excuses nothing and POL-RD-13 has no work to do. The chat message names no road and carries waypoint_hint null, so POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test cannot be run and no distance is excluded under POL-RD-04 or POL-RD-14. The fare is METERED with a null quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 does not close the route, and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is not in play. There is no ERP or surcharge line to correct under POL-RD-09. The billed distance (13.2 km) equals the trace distance, so no DRIVER_COMPENSATION arises under POL-RD-04. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 1 against 207 completed trips in 90 days is far below POL-RD-06's three-flag or 0.05-ratio pattern test, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift on a future ruling and no driver-conduct referral. No clause produces a referral here, so the referrals list is empty.

Confidence is 0.9, capped by the deciding artifact EV-TRIP-02838 at weight 1.0, which carries the amendment timestamp and the missing re-quote.

What would resolve it. The reviewer needs the amended drop-off re-quote — the platform's optimal distance and duration between the pickup and the amended drop-off pin (amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min) — or confirmation that the mid-trip pin move did not affect the driven route. With that figure POL-RD-05 can run, the excess can be re-baselined with pre-amendment distance excluded, and the ordinary POL-RD-02 arithmetic can be applied; without it the excess cannot be measured against the correct baseline.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
